objective: Learners build a preparation checklist and question list for a fictional dentist appointment in two rounds, first with modeled sentence starters and then with that support removed, covering what to bring and what to ask.
scenario: A fictional character has a routine cleaning appointment at Willow Creek Dental next week. In Round 1, the learner completes a preparation checklist and a question list using sentence starters provided on this task sheet. In Round 2, the learner repeats both kinds of preparation for a second fictional appointment, a follow-up X-ray visit at the same office, this time without the sentence starters.
materials: the two fictional appointment scenarios printed on this task sheet

tasks.directions: Think broadly about appointment preparation before building a specific checklist.

prompts.text: Name two things almost any medical or dental appointment might require a visitor to bring or know ahead of time, without listing anything specific to Willow Creek Dental yet.

tasks.directions: Complete the Round 1 checklist for the fictional routine cleaning appointment using the sentence starters below.

prompts.text: I completed the sentence starter 'I will bring my ___ card so the front desk can check me in.'
I completed the sentence starter 'One question I want to ask the dentist is ___.'
Using the sentence starter 'I should arrive ___ minutes early because ___,' explain how early you would plan to arrive for this fictional appointment and why.

tasks.directions: Repeat the same two kinds of preparation for the second fictional appointment, the follow-up X-ray visit, this time without sentence starters.

prompts.text: For the fictional follow-up X-ray appointment at Willow Creek Dental, write your own preparation checklist from scratch: list at least three things to bring or confirm ahead of time, then write at least two original questions you would ask the dental staff about the X-ray visit, without reusing the sentence starters from Round 1.

tasks.directions: Compare how Round 1 and Round 2 felt to complete.

prompts.text: Which round felt more natural to complete, Round 1 with sentence starters or Round 2 without them, and what does that tell you about which parts of appointment preparation you already do automatically?

remediation: If a learner's Round 2 checklist stays generic ('bring stuff'), reteach by returning to the Round 1 sentence starters together and having the learner verbally restate each one in their own words before writing the Round 2 list independently.
extension: Have the learner create a third preparation checklist for a fictional eye exam appointment, noting which items stay the same across all three appointment types and which are specific to each.
